title: Small Tools
subtitle: Small repositories I authored or contributed to for engineering, research, job-search materials, and agent collaboration. They come from recurring workflow problems: context drift, scattered research, repeated resume maintenance, and the need to bring agents into tasks reliably.
viewAllDescription: Browse the small tools behind my context management, research, and agent collaboration workflows.

project-context-meta-skill.title: Project Context Meta-Skill
project-context-meta-skill.summary: A personal meta-skill for building and managing AI-native engineering environments. Through three decoupled subsystems, it provides structured project-level context management and shapes the AI into an engineer that can question, reason, and weigh trade-offs independently.
points: Uses structured project memory to prevent the AI from forgetting information that has already been emphasized or repeating mistakes it has already made in long conversations.
Preserves raw requirements and specifications so the AI can understand the user's root goals and original intent, anchoring exploration when information is incomplete or the task is open-ended.

Makes the AI aware that users cannot always express requirements clearly, so it should guide and challenge the user when appropriate, reason from the root goal and code implementation, offer its own trade-offs, and avoid over-engineered complexity.
Indirectly preserves task-specific prompts so they can be traced, migrated, and learned from.
Captures the problems and reflections I accumulated while using AI tools.

research-skills.title: Engineering Research Skills
research-skills.summary: A research workflow for engineering, product, market, and scientific judgment. It targets situations where the question is broad, the information is noisy, and the final output still needs to support a decision.
points: Turns ad hoc searching into a reusable process across Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, and similar AI tools.
Uses AnySearch as the default real-time retrieval entry point for technical selection, product opportunity analysis, competitor research, and paper or open-source evaluation.
Requires outputs to include not only collected facts, but also evidence, boundaries, risks, and actionable recommendations.

Compresses uncertain information environments into engineering material that can be discussed, decided on, and carried forward, ultimately giving practical guidance for the user's decisions and implementation.

latex-resume.title: LaTeX Resume Builder
latex-resume.summary: A private in-progress resume project exploring how to generate multilingual, role-targeted resumes with LaTeX. It addresses a real maintenance problem: the same experience needs different language variants, role emphasis, and length constraints without drifting out of sync.
points: Explores structured content for Chinese, English, and other variants by separating experience content, project descriptions, skill phrasing, and layout control.
Targets fast adaptation for different roles by changing the emphasis across projects, skills, and experience without manually rebuilding each file.
Uses LaTeX for stable formatting and version control, making the resume closer to a long-lived content asset than a one-off document.
May eventually become a skill, template system, or another automation tool for a reusable job-search material workflow.

anysearch-skill.title: AnySearch Skill
anysearch-skill.summary: A unified real-time search engine skill for AI Agents, supporting general web search, vertical domain search, parallel batch search, and full-page web content extraction.
points: AnySearch provides foundational search capability to AI Agents through an API, focusing on search quality, speed, and customizability.
Supports multiple runtimes including Python, Node.js, PowerShell, and Shell to reduce integration friction across systems and agent environments.
Fixed the agent's discovery and invocation of Python scripts; the contribution has been merged upstream.

crater-prompt.title: Crater Agent Prompts
crater-prompt.summary: A set of agent working prompts accumulated for Crater development before the formal Skill mechanism became popular. It came from a concrete need: helping AI quickly understand a complex project's engineering context, collaboration rules, and development constraints instead of relearning the project background from scratch every time.
points: Turns Crater development experience, recurring requirements, and collaboration habits into working instructions that can be given directly to AI.
Helps agents enter the existing engineering context faster, reducing invalid implementation or repeated communication caused by missing project constraints.
Although mostly document-oriented, it served as an early tool by externalizing implicit experience into a reusable collaboration entry point.
